{"consolidated_memory":"DROPPED FRAMES IN realtime/ws/session.ts — THREE SEPARATE INCIDENTS

**OCCASION 1: [2026-01-11] Non-ASCII Name Records**
- Component: realtime/ws/session.ts (realtime side)
- Problem: Dropped frames in websocket session
- Manifestation: Affected records carrying non-ASCII names
- Repro: Hold a socket open through a network flap
- Root cause: Listener registered but never removed
- Signal: Frames missing from the client sequence
- Measurement: Cold start performance degraded 20 percent to 741 ms
- Fix: Removed the listener on teardown and asserted it in a test
- PR #3134, branch fix/dropped-frames-1
- Note: Same corner of realtime/ws/session.ts as earlier dropped frames work, so context carried over

**OCCASION 2: [2026-06-21] Negative UTC Offset Users**
- Component: realtime/ws/session.ts (realtime side)
- Problem: Dropped frames in websocket session
- Manifestation: Affected users sitting in a negative UTC offset
- Repro: Hold a socket open through a network flap
- Root cause: Clock skew between the two hosts
- Signal: Frames missing from the client sequence
- Measurement: Backlog cleared 78 minutes after the deploy
- Fix: Switched the deadline to a monotonic clock
- PR #5010, branch fix/dropped-frames-2
- Stack: TypeScript
- Test coverage: realtime/ws/session.test.ts

**OCCASION 3: [2026-08-26] Five Percent Rollout Bucket**
- Component: realtime/ws/session.ts (realtime side)
- Problem: Dropped frames in websocket session
- Manifestation: Affected accounts in the five percent rollout bucket
- Repro: Hold a socket open through a network flap
- Root cause: Connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Signal: Frames missing from the client sequence
- Measurement: Nightly rollup matched the source counts for 44 days running (sustained improvement)
- Fix: Raised the pool ceiling and put a bounded wait queue in front of it
- PR #7986, branch fix/dropped-frames-3
- Stack: TypeScript
- Test coverage: realtime/ws/session.test.ts"}
